about_data.title: About the data
about_data.lede: Everything we publish comes from official open data portals, transformed with a documented methodology and no editorial layer.
about_data.sources_intro: These are the official sources that feed the platform:
about_data.neutrality_body_1: Hola Política is civic infrastructure, not an opinion platform. These are the lines we draw:
about_data.neutrality_body_2: If at any point you see content that looks editorial or one-sided, it's a bug. Let us know.
about_data.correction_body: If you find a data error (mislabeled vote, misclassified deputy, outdated profile) or a privacy issue, write to us. We resolve each case with traceability: we identify the source, fix it, and if the error came from the official source we forward the feedback.
about_data.rgpd_body_1: We process data on people who exercise public functions under the public-interest legal basis for transparency and journalistic purposes (Art. 85 GDPR, Art. 28 LO 3/2018, Spanish Transparency Act 19/2013). We never show private data, only mandate-related information.
about_data.rgpd_body_2: If you believe the treatment of public data about your parliamentary activity is inappropriate in our context, write to us and we evaluate each case individually.
about_data.cta_body: The project is open source. To collaborate, report bugs or suggest improvements, start with the project page.

about.title: About the project
about.why_body: In representative democracies, citizens don't vote directly on laws: we delegate that decision to the people we elect every four years. The compact works if we can see what our representatives do with that mandate, which laws they approve, which they reject, who proposes them, how each group votes. This platform centralises that information in one place, open and downloadable, so any citizen or journalist can follow it without navigating scattered official portals.
about.mission_body: Open civic platform that centralises votes, initiatives and parliamentary activity from Spanish chambers. Lets journalists and citizens see how each representative or group voted, with no intermediaries and no political interpretation.
about.principle_body: The project is neutral civic infrastructure. It issues no opinions or assessments about the votes, only verifiable data. Comparative metrics across groups or representatives are always shown in full (every pair, both ends of the range) to avoid one-sided narratives.
about.coverage_phase3: Phase 3, Barcelona City Council Plenary, coming.
about.licence_body: Code under EUPL-1.2. Data under CC-BY 4.0. The project is open source and contributions are welcome.
about.api_intro: Everything you see here is available to journalists, researchers and citizens through a documented REST API. No keys, no signup, no arbitrary limits. Data is published under CC-BY 4.0.
about.api_dump_intro: For academic analysis and data journalism, we expose dump endpoints that return a full dataset in a single request:
about.api_dump_deputies: Active representatives in a legislature with their group and constituency.
about.api_dump_votes: Every vote in a legislature with aggregate counts (Aye/No/Abst/Absent). Optional date range filter.
about.api_dump_vote_records: Each representative's individual vote on ONE specific vote (id passed in). Split out to avoid downloads of hundreds of thousands of records in a single request.
about.api_dump_initiatives: Every initiative in a legislature with its topic classification.
about.api_rate_limit_body: No hard limits today. We ask consumers to keep a reasonable pace. For recurring bulk loads or intensive academic use, contact us to coordinate periodic dataset copies.
about.glossary_intro: Parliamentary language is technical. Here are the terms you'll encounter most often, in plain language.

glossary_terms.definition: A law proposed by the Government. If approved, it becomes binding law. The main path by which the Government legislates.
A law proposed by a parliamentary group (not the Government). If approved, it becomes binding law.

glossary_terms.term: Proposición no de Ley / PNL (Non-binding motion)
glossary_terms.definition: A NON-binding proposal. Asks the Government to do something but does not change the law. If approved, it's a political mandate without direct legal force. The most frequent kind of plenary vote.
An emergency norm with the force of law issued by the Government. Congress must ratify (accept) or repeal (annul) it within 30 days.
After an urgent question to the Government (interpelación), a group can table a motion demanding a specific position. Politically binding, not legally.
Congress's decision on a Government RDL: convalidar = accept, derogar = annul.
% of a group's members voting the same way. 100% cohesion means perfect voting discipline; lower numbers signal cross-cutting votes.
% of votes where two groups voted the same way (Aye, No or Abstain).

glossary.Proposició de Llei: Legislative initiative filed by parliamentary groups in the Congress.
glossary.Projecte de Llei: Legislative initiative filed by the Government.
glossary.Proposició no de Llei (PNL): Political agreement with no legal effect, Congress takes a stance towards the Government or other institutions.
glossary.Proposició no de Llei: Political agreement with no legal effect, Congress takes a stance towards the Government or other institutions.
glossary.Reial Decret-llei: Norm with the force of law issued by the Government on grounds of urgency. Congress must ratify or repeal it within 30 days.
glossary.Real Decreto-ley: Norm with the force of law issued by the Government on grounds of urgency. Congress must ratify or repeal it within 30 days.
glossary.Moció: After an urgent question to the Government (interpelación), a group may table a motion asking for a specific position.
glossary.Interpel·lació: Urgent question put by Congress to the Government on a specific political matter.
glossary.Reforma d'Estatut: Amendment of an Autonomy Statute. Special legislative procedure in Congress.
glossary.Cohesió de grup: Percentage of group members who vote the same way in a given vote.
glossary.Dissidència: An MP voting differently from the majority line of their group.
glossary.Coincidència: Percentage of votes in which two groups (or two MPs) voted the same way.
glossary.Esmena: Amendment proposed to a text in the pipeline, before the final vote.
glossary.Tramitació en lectura única: Fast-track procedure, no committee stage, debated directly in plenary.
glossary.Quòrum: Minimum attendance required for a vote to be valid.
glossary.Veto del Senat: Formal rejection of a law passed by Congress. To override it, Congress must approve the text by absolute majority, or wait two months and vote it through by simple majority.
glossary.Veto del Senado: Formal rejection of a law passed by Congress. To override it, Congress must approve the text by absolute majority, or wait two months and vote it through by simple majority.
glossary.Esmena del Senat: Amendment proposed by the Senate to a text passed by Congress. The Senate may accept, reject or amend bills sent by Congress; amendments return to Congress for ratification or veto.
glossary.Enmienda del Senado: Amendment proposed by the Senate to a text passed by Congress. The Senate may accept, reject or amend bills sent by Congress; amendments return to Congress for ratification or veto.
glossary.Lectura única: Fast-track procedure for a law: it goes straight to plenary debate without a committee stage. Reserved for urgent or broadly agreed texts.
glossary.Avocació al ple: Decision by the plenary to take an initiative out of its committee and pass it directly.
glossary.Avocación al pleno: Decision by the plenary to take an initiative out of its committee and pass it directly.
glossary.Convalidació: Approval by Congress of a government Real Decreto-ley, giving it the force of standing law.
glossary.Convalidación: Approval by Congress of a government Real Decreto-ley, giving it the force of standing law.
glossary.Derogació: Repeal by Congress of a government Real Decreto-ley within the 30 days following its entry into force.
glossary.Derogación: Repeal by Congress of a government Real Decreto-ley within the 30 days following its entry into force.
glossary.Vots emesos: Share of votes in which the MP cast a ballot (Yes, No or Abstain) out of the total votes during their term. Excludes justified absences (medical leave, parental leave). Votes cast as a minister or government member are counted according to parliamentary convention. See /about/data for the full methodology.
glossary.Votes cast: Share of votes in which the MP cast a ballot (Yes, No or Abstain) out of the total votes during their term. Excludes justified absences (medical leave, parental leave). Votes cast as a minister or government member are counted according to parliamentary convention. See /about/data for the full methodology.

lifecycle.title: How a law is made in the Congress
lifecycle.intro: These are the eight stages a legislative initiative goes through in the Spanish Congress of Deputies. Each stage is defined in the Congress's Standing Orders; the votes you'll see on the site can correspond to any of them.
lifecycle.caveat: Steps 6 and 7 only apply to initiatives that reach the Senate. Non-binding motions (PNL) follow a shorter path: they go straight to the plenary for debate and a vote.

presentation.title: Filing
presentation.body: A parliamentary group or the Government files the initiative: Proposición de Ley (groups) or Proyecto de Ley (Government).

qualification.title: Qualification
qualification.body: The Bureau of Congress admits the text and assigns it to the competent committee.

totality_debate.title: Debate on the whole text
totality_debate.body: The plenary debates the text as a whole and may veto it (reject it) or admit it into processing.

committee.title: Committee stage
committee.body: The committee studies the text, hears experts and drafts amendments to the articles.

plenary_final.title: Final plenary vote
plenary_final.body: The plenary votes on the final text with the amendments incorporated.

senate.title: Senate
senate.body: The text moves to the Senate, which may approve it unchanged, amend it or veto it.

return.title: Back to Congress
return.body: If the Senate amends or vetoes, the text returns to Congress, which ratifies its text or accepts the amendments.

publication.title: Publication in the BOE
publication.body: Once approved, the law is published in the State Official Gazette and enters into force.
